mission.brief: Prepare a factual handover for fictional ash-03: put all four dated records from history.txt into handover.txt in chronological order, including the missing sample and capacity/units. Omit the context header. Display the original and final report with cat after writing. Self-review the observed growth, uncertainty and recommended next checks; your prose and forecast are not automatically assessed.
constraints: SIMULATOR: supplied synthetic snapshots of fictional hosts, not measurements of your computer or VM. No free, vmstat, df, processes, mounts, repairs or cleanup commands are simulated here.

Score checks factual report bytes, reading evidence and preserved sources only. Interpretation, uncertainty and recommended next checks require self-review; 100/100 is NOT proof of diagnostic mastery.

Type help for supported text commands. For this lab's context, worked interpretation and common mistakes, read HELP.txt with cat. This reference is available in both modes; it contains no repair command.

Only declared report files can be written. > truncates before reading; >> appends. Errors do not undo writes. Finish all report writes before reading sources and final reports: any actual write clears earlier reading evidence.

Keep source record spelling, units, order and final LF exactly in reports. Equivalent supported paths and filters count for report construction. Required reading evidence specifically uses cat on each source and final report after the last write; other tools do not satisfy cat inspections. Reasoning is self-reviewed. Reset preserves history.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR HELP — trend handover
This is synthetic historical data, not monitoring. All timestamps use fixed-width ISO dates in UTC and capacity is fixed. The missing row means no measurement, not zero usage.
Self-review: what changed across observed dates? Is the apparent rate stable enough for a forecast? Which checks should the next operator make?
Model interpretation: observed usage rose 640 to 736 GiB over three days. The endpoint average is 32 GiB/day, but this arithmetic is NOT checked and the missing interior sample prevents assuming uniform daily growth. Four records, including one absent observation, are insufficient for a reliable exhaustion date. Gather a longer comparable series, check workload/retention changes, capacity and inode trends, and confirm alert policy. Retain the gap in any handover.
Common mistakes: dropping a missing sample; treating it as zero; assuming lexical sort is numeric sort for arbitrary values; extrapolating a stable growth rate from too few points.
Automatically checked: exact four sorted records, original/report reading and preservation. Handover reasoning, forecast and operational recommendation are self-reviewed; no semantic grader exists. Type help for commands.
Required checked reading actions use cat on each source and final report after the last write. Other text tools may construct reports but do not satisfy these cat actions.
